conventions.convention: Ordinary attention uses row-token matrices and row softmax; every masked query row must have at least one allowed key.
The causal mask permits j ≤ i, including the diagonal. Sinusoidal encoding positions and feature coordinates start at zero.
Sequence-limit models append a fixed end marker and read its final state. Hard attention chooses the smallest maximizing key index; maps, depth and head count are fixed independently of length.

The inverse-length soft-influence result assumes additive bounded token and positional embeddings, fixed linear query/key/value maps, and globally Lipschitz positionwise maps. The changed token must precede the final marker.
The PCFG prefix law conditions on reaching the sampled prefix length, without conditioning on exact total length. Eventual-termination conditioning replaces p by min(p,1-p).

Yun expressivity blocks use column-token matrices, column softmax, two size-one heads, width-four residual ReLU feedforward sublayers, a permitted scalar query bias, and no layer normalization. Modified lookup hardmax distributes weight equally among maximizers.
Universality fixes d ≥ 1, n ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ p < ∞, uses integrated Lebesgue Lp error under Countable Choice, and permits depth and parameters to depend on the target and tolerance.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated fixed-model and bounded-support hypotheses, any smaller positive free-position fraction can be retained while absorbing one attention layer into new layer-zero activations of bounded support; iteration through fixed depth leaves the output dependent on only constantly many original positions.

For two length-n inputs satisfying the bounded additive dot-product soft-attention hypotheses and differing only at i < n, their final hidden states differ by at most C/n; a fixed globally Lipschitz logit map followed by softmax gives probability-vector distance at most C'/n.

For the stated integer grids with n ≤ δ^(-d), modified two-head residual attention and three-piece scalar gates realize every equivariant table on distinct-column grid matrices, returning zero on duplicate-column and sentinel inputs; position-tagged grids admit arbitrary tables.

The survival-conditioned PCFG prefix law has equal-mass pairs differing at a nonfinal unmatched opening, with paired-event mass at least p²(1-p); conditioning on eventual termination gives the same process with parameter min(p,1-p).
For probability vectors r,s,q,q' on an alphabet of size m, if ||q-q'||₁ ≤ ε, then CE(r,q)/2 + CE(s,q')/2 ≥ H((r+s)/2) - log(1+mε).

Every finite composition of position-shared, position-free encoder layers with unmasked multi-head self-attention satisfies T(PX)=PT(X); simultaneous mask permutation gives the corresponding masked identity.

Assuming Countable Choice, fixed d ≥ 1, n ≥ 2 and finite p ≥ 1, ordinary Yun blocks approximate continuous compactly supported equivariant maps in global integrated Lp; trainable positional encodings approximate arbitrary continuous maps on compact domains in integrated Lp over that domain.
Attention is row-softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V; additive masks use zero on allowed pairs and negative infinity otherwise, with at least one allowed key per row.

concerns.concern: The Statement says “row softmax adds O(n²),” and Proof 2.1 counts only n rows of n scores after summing over h heads. The defined multi-head implementation has h separate n-by-n score matrices, so its softmax work is O(hn²). No fixed-h qualification is stated; taking h=d with size-one heads exposes the missing factor. The combined O(n²d) interaction bound survives because positive head widths imply h ≤ d, but the separate softmax claim as written is overstrong.

Proof 4.1 infers vanishing transition-strip error because “the fixed finite network is bounded,” while the ramp network changes with ρ and the softmax scales also vary. Boundedness for each individual network does not itself supply the uniform output bound needed for that inference. The particular construction appears to permit a short uniform-bound argument: quantizer outputs stay bounded, softmax outputs are convex combinations, and the lookup pulse/detector gates have bounded amplitudes independently of ramp width. That bound and the parameter-selection order should be made explicit.

seams_checked.note: The actual item edges use def-feedforward-neural-network for finite shared positionwise maps and layered MLP conventions. Its definition and diagram agree with those uses. The separate single-hidden-layer universality theorem is not imported.

This is contextual page sequencing. The foundation-model definition imports no attention theorem and explicitly avoids restricting foundation models to a particular architecture or asserting transfer guarantees.

The block-summary definition and tiled algorithm preserve row-softmax weighted values and nonempty allowed-key sets. Their arbitrary real score scale is explicitly supplied; standard scaled dot-product attention is its c=1/√d specialization.

The page requirement is contextual. The adapter definition concerns a finite linear map with a frozen base and trainable factors; it makes no logical use of attention universality or sequence-limit results and does not strengthen them.
